newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonia, Scandinavia solve flight row.
newsitem.headline: Estonia, Scandinavia solve flight row.

text.p: Estonia has solved its row with aviation officials from Scandinavia and new winter flight plans have been agreed, Estonian officials said on Thursday.
The row threatened to halt Scandinavian Airlines flights to Estonia but the summer timetable was extended last week to allow flights to continue.

The Estonian aviation authority said in a statement that Estonian Transport Minister Kalev Kukk and Danish counterpart Jan Troejborg agreed that Estonian Air, majority owned by Danish carrier Maersk, will have six flights a week to Copenhagen and that SAS will have 10.
SAS will also have nine flights a week between Tallinn and Stockholm and Estonian Air 12.
The exact timetable has still to be fixed by the airlines.
The new arrangements are more or less in line with the airlines' demands before the row began.

The arguing was sparked by Estonia's request to SAS to cut its flights between Copenhagen and the Estonian capital Tallinn to one a day from two as it wanted to resume Estonian Air flights between the two cities.
It also refused to allow SAS to fly twice a day between Stockholm and Tallinn instead of once a day.
